heard: A rushed political deadline forced the world's largest airship skyward. In October 1930, Britain's R-101 departed for India on its maiden voyage. To boost lift, designers had hastily sliced in an extra gas cell. Air Minister Lord Thompson boarded despite storm warnings and mist trials. Gales over France forced the giant into two steep fatal dives. The hydrogen ignited instantly, killing 48 people inside the blazing hull. The only survivors were engineers riding in external engine cars. Yet the Empire demanded a triumph, ignoring every warning.
